info.title: Optical Character Recognition
info.description:
The Optical Character Recognition API enables you to extract information from portfolio statements that are formatted as PDFs or images. 
Using the API, you can retrieve the following details from a portfolio statement:
* Names of securities.
* Ticker symbols.
* Share quantities.
* Market value.

The API works asynchronously. A statement PDF or image is uploaded to the API using an initial POST call to  the `statement-details` endpoint. This call returns a unique job ID which is appended to the URL of subsequent GET calls to the same endpoint. These GET calls return the holdings information parsed from the statement.

When uploading a statement for processing, you need to identify the custodian that the statement was received from.  You use the `custodians` endpoint to retrieve identifiers for supported custodians.

get.description: Get all custodians for the language and region specified in the `Accept-Language` header.</br></br>The response returns the unique `documentName` and `documentShortName` values that identify custodians. At least one of these values is required when making a POST request to the `statement-details` endpoint. </br></br>The response separates the supported custodians into two lists. The `mainCustodians` list contains custodians for whom specific processing logic has been written.  The `others` list contains custodians for whom common processing logic is used and may therefore produce results with a lower degree of accuracy.

post.description: Extract portfolio statement information from the base64-encoded PDF/image sent in the request. Information is extracted based on the logic defined, where available, for the custodian specified in the `documentShortName` or `documentName` values in the request body.</br></br>The request supports the following file types:</br></br> -JPG </br> -JPEG</br> - PNG </br> - PDF </br></br>When sending a PDF, you can specify the page numbers to extract information from. For example, `1,3,6,9` or `1,3,6,8-11`. If you do not specify `pageNumbers` values, the whole document will be considered. If you pass a `0` value, it will be considered as `1`. When specifying a range, for example `8-11`, the first number must be smaller than the second number. </br></br>The response contains an `id` which you use to retrieve the results of the request. The `id` can also be used to track the request.

fileName.description: Name of file used to store image/pdf object

pageNumbers.description: Comma-separated list of PDF page numbers to process

documentShortName.description: Short name of a custodian. If not present, passes to 'DEFAULT'.

get.description:
Get the portfolio statement information extracted by the `POST /statement-details` request. </br></br>The unique job ID returned by the POST request is automatically included in this GET request's URL. 
</br></br>The response contains a JSON obect with an array of security details such as ticker, name, market value, and so on.

404.description: Resource you requested is not found.
